searchText: > seems like go-etheruem full nodes are not capable of doing debug_traceTransaction when the transaction happened like 300+ blocks in past You just need to specify a reexec-option. And then geth might have to go back another couple of thousand blocks, to find a state that was flushed to disk, and then it will chug through those thousand blocks again to wind up at the state you need By default, it's pretty low, to prevent trivial non-intentional DoS when people doesn't realise that the calll may cause the node to re-execute 20K blocks

excerpts.author: holiman
excerpts.content:
> seems like go-etheruem full nodes are not capable of doing debug_traceTransaction when the transaction happened like 300+ blocks in past

You just need to specify a reexec-option. And then geth might have to go back another couple of thousand blocks, to find a state that was flushed to disk, and then it will chug through those thousand blocks again to wind up at the state you need
